title: GATE CS Topic Test — Operating Systems (Set 2)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — Operating Systems (Set 2)

questions.questionTextEn: A C program executes the statement `fork(); fork(); fork();` (3 consecutive `fork()` calls, all succeeding). How many TOTAL processes exist after all 3 calls complete (including the original parent process)?
questions.explanationEn: Each `fork()` doubles the number of processes: `2^3 = 8` total processes (1 original parent + 7 newly created processes).

questions.questionTextEn: A paging system uses a 4 KB (4096-byte) page size. A process requires 10,000 bytes of memory. How many bytes of internal fragmentation occur in its allocated pages?
questions.explanationEn: Pages allocated = `ceil(10000 / 4096) = 3` pages = `3 × 4096 = 12,288` bytes. Internal fragmentation = `12,288 - 10,000 = 2,288` bytes.

questions.questionTextEn: A disk head is initially at cylinder 50. Pending requests arrive in order: `80, 30, 90, 20`. What is the total head movement (in cylinders) under FCFS disk scheduling?
Which of the following actions are typically performed by the OS kernel during a full process context switch between two different processes P1 and P2?
optionsEn: Saving P1's CPU registers and Program Counter into P1's PCB
Switching the page table base register (e.g., CR3 on x86) to P2's page table
Loading P2's registers and Program Counter from P2's PCB
questions.explanationEn: Switching between distinct processes requires saving/restoring CPU state in PCBs and updating the address space (page table base register, often flushing non-tagged TLB entries).

questions.questionTextEn: External fragmentation occurs in contiguous variable-partition memory allocation and segmentation, whereas pure paging eliminates external fragmentation and instead suffers only from:
optionsEn: Internal fragmentation (in the last page of a process)
questions.explanationEn: In paging, any free frame can be assigned to any process (no external fragmentation), but the last page of a process may only be partially filled, causing internal fragmentation averaging half a page.

questions.questionTextEn: A counting semaphore `S` is initialized to 7. After 15 `wait(S)` (P) operations and 10 `signal(S)` (V) operations complete (assuming no process remains permanently blocked), what is the final value of `S`?
questions.explanationEn: Each `wait` decrements `S` by 1 and each `signal` increments `S` by 1. Final value = `7 - 15 + 10 = 2`.

questions.questionTextEn: A system uses 32-bit virtual addresses and a page size of 4 KB (4096 bytes). How many bits are used for the Virtual Page Number (VPN)?
questions.explanationEn: Page offset = `log2(4096) = 12` bits. VPN bits = `32 - 12 = 20` bits.

questions.questionTextEn: A paged memory system has a TLB hit rate of 90%, TLB lookup time of 10 ns, and main memory access time of 100 ns (assuming a single-level page table and no page faults). What is the Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT) in nanoseconds?
questions.explanationEn: TLB hit takes `10 + 100 = 110 ns`. TLB miss takes `10 + 100 (page table) + 100 (data) = 210 ns`. EMAT = `0.90(110) + 0.10(210) = 99 + 21 = 120 ns`.

questions.questionTextEn: Which CPU scheduling algorithm minimizes the average waiting time for a given set of processes arriving simultaneously (assuming burst times are known)?
questions.explanationEn: By an exchange argument, scheduling shorter jobs before longer jobs minimizes cumulative waiting time across all subsequent processes, making SJF provably optimal for average waiting time.

questions.questionTextEn: Imposing a strict global numbering on all resource types and requiring every process to request resources only in strictly increasing order of their numbers prevents deadlock by breaking which condition?
questions.explanationEn: If every resource acquisition moves strictly upward in the global order, no cycle of waiting processes can ever form, eliminating Circular Wait.

questions.topicTag: OS — Memory Allocation (Best Fit vs First Fit)
questions.questionTextEn: Free memory partitions of sizes `100 KB, 500 KB, 200 KB, 300 KB, 600 KB` (in order) are available. Processes of sizes `212 KB, 417 KB, 112 KB, 426 KB` arrive in order. Under Best Fit, which process (if any) CANNOT be allocated?
questions.explanationEn: Best Fit: `212 KB -> 300 KB` (88 left); `417 KB -> 500 KB` (83 left); `112 KB -> 200 KB` (88 left); `426 KB -> 600 KB` (174 left). All four processes fit!

questions.questionTextEn: In a Unix-like filesystem, which of the following statements comparing hard links and symbolic (soft) links are TRUE?
optionsEn: A hard link shares the exact same inode number as the original file
Deleting the original filename does NOT delete the file's data blocks as long as at least one hard link remains
A symbolic link can point to a file on a different mounted filesystem, whereas a hard link cannot
Deleting the original file automatically updates all symbolic links to keep working
questions.explanationEn: Hard links increment the inode's link count (A, B) and are confined to one filesystem; symlinks store a path string and can cross filesystems (C) but become dangling links if the target is deleted (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: In a Round Robin scheduler, the time quantum is `q = 20 ms` and each context switch takes `2 ms`. Assuming all processes are CPU-bound with bursts much larger than `q`, what percentage of CPU time is wasted on context switching? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: Each cycle takes `20 + 2 = 22 ms`, of which 2 ms is overhead. Wasted percentage = `(2 / 22) × 100% = 9.09%`.
Total processes = `2^4 = 16`, so newly created child processes = `16 - 1 = 15`.

questions.questionTextEn:
A system has 3 resource types (A, B, C) with Available = (3, 3, 2). Five processes have (Allocation | Max):
P0: (0,1,0) | (7,5,3)
P1: (2,0,0) | (3,2,2)
P2: (3,0,2) | (9,0,2)
P3: (2,1,1) | (2,2,2)
P4: (0,0,2) | (4,3,3)
Which of the following is a VALID safe sequence?
questions.explanationEn: Needs (Max - Alloc): P0=(7,4,3), P1=(1,2,2), P2=(6,0,0), P3=(0,1,1), P4=(4,3,1). With Avail=(3,3,2), P1 runs -> Avail=(5,3,2); P3 runs -> Avail=(7,4,3); P4 runs -> Avail=(7,4,5); P2 runs -> Avail=(10,4,7); P0 runs. Thus `<P1, P3, P4, P2, P0>` is safe.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 3-frame Clock page replacement algorithm, frames currently hold pages `[A(R=1), B(R=1), C(R=0)]` with the clock hand pointing at `A`. A page fault occurs for page `D`. How many reference bits are cleared from 1 to 0 before a victim frame is chosen?
questions.explanationEn: Hand checks `A` (R=1 -> clear to 0, advance), checks `B` (R=1 -> clear to 0, advance), checks `C` (R=0 -> evict `C`). Two reference bits are cleared.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about hardware and OS synchronization primitives are TRUE?
optionsEn: Spinlocks waste CPU cycles via busy waiting, making them suitable mainly for very short critical sections on multiprocessors
A binary semaphore can be used to enforce both mutual exclusion and ordering/signaling between threads
Monitors encapsulate shared data and condition variables, allowing at most one thread active inside the monitor at a time
Disabling interrupts in user mode is the standard way to implement user-space mutexes on modern multi-core CPUs
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are true. User-mode programs cannot disable interrupts (privileged instruction), and disabling interrupts on one core doesn't stop other cores anyway (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Three processes P1, P2, P3 arrive at t = 0 with burst times 5, 3, and 4 ms. Under Round Robin with time quantum `q = 2 ms` (order P1, P2, P3), what is the completion time of P1?
questions.explanationEn: Gantt: P1(0-2, rem 3), P2(2-4, rem 1), P3(4-6, rem 2), P1(6-8, rem 1), P2(8-9, done), P3(9-11, done), P1(11-12, done). P1 completes at t = 12 ms.

questions.questionTextEn: A counting semaphore `S` is initialized to 10. Processes perform 18 `P(S)` (wait) operations and 5 `V(S)` (signal) operations in sequence. What is the resulting integer value of `S` (using standard negative-value semantics)?
questions.explanationEn: `S = 10 - 18 + 5 = -3` (indicating 3 processes are currently blocked in the semaphore queue).

questions.questionTextEn: In a bounded-buffer Producer-Consumer system with buffer capacity `N = 8`, initially `empty = 8`, `full = 0`, `mutex = 1`. After 5 items are produced and 2 items are consumed, what is the value of `empty + full`?
questions.explanationEn: At any quiescent point outside critical sections, `empty = 8 - 5 + 2 = 5` and `full = 0 + 5 - 2 = 3`, preserving the invariant `empty + full = N = 8`.
